newsitem.title: USA: U.S. General backs joint Army training of sexes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. General backs joint Army training of sexes.

text.p: The U.S. Army's training chief on Wednesday rejected calls for separate training of men and women recruits despite a major sexual scandal that has uncovered "a few bad apples" among male drill sergeants.

"I do believe in gender-integrated training. We don't want to go backwards. I don't have any evidence that tells me that we need to go backwards," Gen. William Hartzog said of demands by some in Congress to end joint training of the sexes.

Hartzog, head of the Army Training and Doctrine Command, told reporters that recent convictions of drill sergeants at Aberdeen Training Ground, Maryland, and other bases for rape and harassment of female recruits had not changed his mind.

"Nothing has changed my mind on the fact that there were a few bad apples," he said in response to questions, noting that the Army did not believe that training effectiveness had been harmed by bad publicity from the scandal.
"I don't believe, and there is no indication in any of the inspections that are going on, that basic training in its basic form is broken in any way," Hartzog said.
The U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force each train their men and women jointly while the Marine Corps, comprised mostly of combat troops, conducts separate training for young males and females.
Some members of Congress, alarmed at the Army scandal, have called on the Army to return to gender-segregated training.
